transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been having these nights where I eat a lot. More than I mean to. Like after grading papers, I’ll start with leftovers and then it just… keeps going—cereal, crackers, peanut butter, classroom snacks. It kind of scares me.
After these episodes of overeating, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself sick, exercising a lot more than usual, or not eating later?

Yeah… I don’t usually make myself sick. But after one of those nights I’ll sort of… punish myself, I guess. I’ll skip breakfast and lunch at school, and then I’ll go hike for hours or do extra yoga, even if I feel shaky and really tired.
When you're eating a lot during these episodes, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating?
Yeah… I do. Once I start, it’s like part of me is standing back saying, Joan, just stop now. But I don’t. I just keep opening things and eating until I’m… really uncomfortably full.
Do these episodes of overeating usually happen at night, or during other times of the day as well?
Mostly at night, I think. I mean… that’s when I notice it. After work, when I’m home. I don’t really think it happens the same way during the day.
Do these nighttime eating episodes happen even when you’re not really hungry, or do they usually happen because you feel physically hungry?
I’m… not totally sure. I don’t always check in with whether I’m actually hungry. It just kind of happens at night, I guess.
Do these nighttime eating episodes and the way you feel afterward cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your daily life in any way?

Yeah… it does. I don’t really like admitting that, but my evenings kind of get taken over by it. And weekends too, sometimes.

I’ll be thinking about how to… fix what happened with food, I guess, instead of grading or seeing people. I’m slower getting school stuff done, and when I’m with friends I’m not really there. At work I try really hard to seem normal and put-together, but I’m worried people can tell.
Do you usually feel like you don’t have much of an appetite in the morning, or find that you eat more in the evening than you originally plan to?

I don’t know about the morning appetite part as much. But in the evening… yeah, I end up eating way more than I meant to. Like I’ll start with leftovers after grading, and then it turns into cereal, crackers, peanut butter, snacks I had packed for my classroom… it feels like a scary amount.
Do these nighttime eating episodes happen after you've already gone to sleep and then woken up, or do they usually happen when you're still awake and winding down for the night?
I… I’m not really sure. I think it’s more when I’m still up, but I haven’t paid close attention to it like that.
Have you ever woken up in the middle of the night and found yourself eating, even if you weren’t fully awake?
I don’t think so… not that I’ve noticed. It’s more like I’m already up, or kind of still awake. But I guess I haven’t really tracked it.
Have you ever woken up in the middle of the night and started eating without really being in control of it, or without remembering it clearly the next day?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I don’t remember anything like that happening. If I’m eating, I’m usually aware enough to know I’m doing it, even if it doesn’t feel great.
During these nighttime eating episodes, do you eat a much larger amount of food in a short period of time than most people would eat in a similar situation?

Yes… I think so. It feels like way more than a normal amount. Like I’ll start with leftovers after grading papers, and then it turns into cereal, crackers, peanut butter… snacks I had packed for my classroom. It kind of scares me when I realize how much it was.
Have you ever woken up during the night, and then started eating while you were still half-asleep or not fully aware of what you were doing?
I don’t think so. I might feel tired or sort of out of it, but I’m aware enough to know I’m eating.
Have these nighttime eating episodes ever caused problems in your relationships, at work, or in other important parts of your life?

Yeah… I guess it has. Not in a dramatic way, but… my evenings and weekends end up kind of revolving around fixing or undoing what happened with food. I get behind on grading, and I’m not really present when I’m with friends. At work I’m always trying to seem like I have it together, and that’s… exhausting.
Have these nighttime eating episodes happened almost every night, or are they more occasional?

It’s not every night. But… for the past few months, I don’t think there’s been many weeks where it didn’t happen at least once. And then the next day I usually try to make up for it, like skipping food at school or doing a long walk or extra yoga.
When you're eating a lot during these nighttime episodes, is it in a short amount of time—like within a couple of hours—or does it spread out more gradually over the evening?

It’s usually pretty fast… like once it starts, it’s not just grazing all night. I’ll start with leftovers while I’m grading, and then within maybe an hour or two I’ve gone through cereal, crackers, peanut butter, snacks I had packed for school… more than I meant to.
During these nighttime eating episodes, do you feel like you’re not in control of your eating, like you can’t stop even if you want to?
Yeah… I do. Once I start, it feels like part of me is sort of watching it happen, like, Joan, just stop. But I don’t. I keep opening things and eating until I feel really uncomfortably full.
